summary: Naman P. Ahuja works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture (attested 2018).
Namita Das is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra under Dragyab Lodro, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Minyag Damchö. He served as Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

Nancy Grace Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Columbia University and earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas, Michael Hahn, Somadeva Vasudeva, and Gary A. Tubb.

Nancy Hock is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at UC Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams, and was affiliated with the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson. She held an appointment at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indian historian and archaeologist. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

Naoji Okuyama (b. 1956) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he also served as an assistant and lecturer (~1985–1990), later becoming a professor at Koyasan University (~1996).
Naoki Nabeshima specializes in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2004, he served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, which he also founded.

Naoko Nishimura specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at Tohoku University in 2002, studied under Toshifumi Goto, and later served there as a specialist researcher (attested 2012).

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, later holding a fellowship at Cardiff University and a Chancellor's Fellowship at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford under Sylvain Lévi and Karl Geldner. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (~1974–1979).

Naoya Funahashi (b. 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an appointment at Otani University (attested 1981) and served as a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

Narada Mahathera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He was educated at Ceylon University College and studied under his traditional teacher Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa from approximately 1917 to 1955.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (b. 1924) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961), where he was a Research Fellow, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from approximately 1967 to 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato (b. 1946) is a historian and Indologist. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1974), he held positions at the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies (~1983–1990), Kobe University (~1990–1996), and as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1996–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, with appointments attested in 1974 and 1988.

Natalie Depraz (b. 1964) is a philosopher who studied at the ENS de lettres et sciences humaines, Paris Nanterre University, and St. Sergius Institute. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie (1997), Paris-Sorbonne University (2000), and University of Rouen-Normandy (~2006).
